messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a sweep combining QKV packing + bias/rope epilogue fusion on paged-KV configs (page_size=256). Short seq (<=128) token p50 improved ~8-12%, but for mid sequences (256-768) we hit ~15% tail regressions when batch >= 8. attaching profiler excerpts below.

aj: Can you paste the trace? was KV page faulting or was it kernel choice churn?

maria: paste from nvprof + custom tracer:

```
# model=llama-7b pagedkv page=256
batch=4 seq=64: p50=12.4ms p95=18.2ms gpu_util=73% kernels: fused_attn_qkv_pack (45%), epilogue_bias_rope_fused (30%), memcopy (10%)
batch=8 seq=512: p50=28.1ms p95=52.6ms gpu_util=88% kernels: fallback_attn (40%), epilogue_scalar (35%), page_prefetch (15%)
observed: epilogue fusion reduced kernel count but increased L2 miss rate on mid seq when packing triggers larger shared memory working set.
```

chris: hmm that smells like prefetch + shared-memory pressure. when pack folds q/k/v into wider layout we push epilogue register/shared usage up, which can evict paged-kv prefetch buffers. Did you see an uptick in page fault latency or stall cycles?

maria: yes, stall cycles jumped ~2.6x in the 256-768 range. page fault ISR was rare but L2 load/store latency spiked. also saw more kernel-selector fallback logs: `kernel_picker: switched to generic_flash for seq=512 batch=8`

aj: two ideas: 1) change kernel selection policy to prefer non-packed epilogue at mid seq if predicted shared memory > threshold; 2) update batching heuristic to split big batches for mid seq into smaller micro-batches to avoid shared mem blowup.

sam: agree. we should codify a rule: if (seq >= 256 && batch >= 8 && model_page_size == 256) prefer epilogue=no-fusion or prefer_prefetch=false. Also add a metric to the chooser: estimated_shared_mem_bytes.

chris: can we compute estimated_shared_mem cheaply from q/k/v width and heads? sampler already estimates workspace for kernels — reuse that. Also add a cheap offline microbench to estimate L2 thrash delta per kernel config.

perf-bot: benchmark report generated: https://perf.redwood/internal/bench/3324500123 (run id 2026-03-18-12:34) :bar_chart:

maria: i pushed a quick patch to kernel_picker to add `shared_mem_est` and a soft-threshold for fusion. rolling a canary to staging now. cmd i ran to repro:

```
./run_inference_bench --model=llama-7b --backend=pagkv --page_size=256 --seq=512 --batch=8 --flags="epilogue=fused,pack_qkv=on" --trace=nvprof.out
```

aj: great. also capture `nvmetrics` for L2/tex/cache stats and add them to the rollout dashboard so canary quickly flags regressions.

maria: noted. one more datapoint: when I toggled `pack_qkv=off` but left epilogue fusion on, mid-seq regressions disappeared but small-seq wins dropped to ~3-4%. so packing is the main lever for small-seq speedups.

sam: sounds like we want a hybrid policy: pack_qkv=on for seq<=128, pack_qkv=conditional for 129..512 based on estimated_shared_mem, and pack_qkv=off for >512. Add a metric `pack_overlap_score` so we can A/B quickly.

chris: can we also try a lightweight prefetch backoff: when estimated_shared_mem > X, reduce prefetch depth from 3->1 so we trade absolute throughput for lower L2 pressure. should be quick to implement.

maria: will add prefetch_backoff flag and re-run. planning to log: kernel_choice, shared_mem_est, prefetch_depth, page_fault_count per request.

aj: thanks. action items: maria open PR for chooser changes + telemetry, chris add microbench harness and L2 thrash estimator, sam define threshold sweep and update batching policy, i'll add a dashboard tile for observed tail regressions.

perf-bot: CI microbench queued: job/3324500123-microbench (ETA ~ 35m).

maria: cool. if anyone wants the raw traces ping me and i'll drop a link. :thinking:
